game_concept: A strategy race set in Eldritch Ruins – Cracked Obelisk, a cracked obelisk: the rune scholar must handle crypt crawlers while practicing lists. Core idea – Slice Slicer: Cut lists with slices like items[1:4] to grab exactly the right group.
theme: Eldritch Ruins – Cracked Obelisk: a cracked obelisk
core_gameplay_loop: Construct a solution, execute it, inspect actual state and outputs, then revise until all mission goals pass.
player_objective: Declare float: declare resource as float, apply resource + 8.5, and print each result with %.1f. Dataset 8 starts with [-3, 0, 16, 19]. Match every stream. Use a full main function and a return statement.
controls: Edit the C program. Run tests all streams; Step shows declarations, assignments and output. readInput() is a LogiCade game-port helper declared in logicade.h. This safe practice runtime supports a documented C subset.
win_condition: The executed solution satisfies every output and world-state check.
lose_condition: The available unsuccessful execution checks are exhausted.
assets_style: Shared Kenney CC0 tile and audio assets with deterministic Canvas layouts; assets are not duplicated per game.
duplicate_check_notes: Unique combination of primary mechanic 'Slice Slicer' (Week 7 slot 3), mission type 'Rival Race', and setting 'Cracked Obelisk'. No other file shares this combination; games sharing the mechanic differ in mission/win condition and setting, and games sharing the setting use a different mechanic.
topic: Basic Parts of C and Variable Declarations

tutorial: Read the objective, fixtures and command reference.
Build the circuit or route, or edit the node/adventure program.

source_player_objective: Beat a rival AI to the sealed archway by solving code steps involving slice_ok that move the rune scholar forward.
source_win_condition: Player progress reaches 100% before the rival does (rival speed 0.95).
source_lose_condition: The rival reaches the sealed archway first, or lives reach 0.
hint: Declare before use. float resource = readInput(); creates the named game-port value; printf uses %.1f.
